Claude accounts now get a year-long sign-in, so you no longer have to sign each Claude account in again every four weeks.

**What changed**

- **One sign-in a year instead of one a month.** `setup.cmd claude <key>` now also makes Claude Code's year-long sign-in for that account. If the account's current sign-in still works, that is a single approval in a private browser window.
- **It is checked before it is used.** The tool keeps the year-long sign-in only if Anthropic places it in the same account, and every Claude switch checks it again. The check sends no message and costs nothing.
- **The switch window reminds you two weeks before it runs out.**
- An account that already has a year-long sign-in is left as it is.

**Limits:** a year-long sign-in can only be used for model requests, which is all Hermes needs from it.

**How it was checked:** automated tests for each part; the check was run on a real PC against an existing year-long sign-in, and the hidden terminal that runs Claude Code's sign-in was run there up to the sign-in link.

**After installing:** nothing to restart. Run `setup.cmd claude <key>` once for each Claude account.

The archive, its SHA-256 and the release gates are attached. Technical details are in `docs/release-notes.md`.
